title: Capacity signal debrief — regional demand variance and next steps
content:
Meeting: Capacity signal debrief — weekly infra sync
Date: 2026-04-20
Lead: Maya Chen (Infrastructure capacity lead)
Attendees: Maya Chen, Arjun Patel, Sofia Ruiz, Liam O'Neill, Greta Andersen, on-call SRE rotation

TL;DR:
- Last week we observed a 22% demand spike in APAC (asia-southeast) tied to an unanticipated enterprise customer test run plus higher PLG trial traffic in eu-west. Net fleet utilization rose from 68% to 84% during peak windows.
- Patching the autoscaler hysteresis reduced oscillation in US regions but revealed slot contention in the eu-west pod group (slot starvation between 03:00–06:00 UTC).
- Immediate mitigations: temp reservation of 20 GPUs in asia-southeast and manual ramp of burst pool in eu-west. Mid-term actions focus on improving demand signals and automated hedging rules.

Snapshot metrics (rolling 7 days ending 2026-04-20):
- Global GPU utilization (weighted): 72% avg, 95th percentile 89% during peak hours.
- APAC (asia-southeast): 78% avg, 95th 95% (spike window 13:00–16:00 local) — increased by +22% week-over-week.
- EU (eu-west): 81% avg during UTC overnight window; p95 latency for small-chat endpoints rose by ~120ms correlating with slot contention.
- US (us-west/us-east): stable utilization 60–70%; autoscaler smoothing reduced thrash by ~40%.

Incidents & observations:
- Slot leak hypothesis (INF-4223): observed tasks not releasing allocated slots after failed container pulls; correlated with eu-west contention. Logs indicate intermittent Docker image pull errors after node kernel update.
- Autoscaler tuning: reducing scale-down aggressiveness fixed thrash but makes temporary over-provisioning costlier; need cost-bound safety nets.
- Prefix cache pressure: higher PLG trials increased cache miss-rate on large-context jobs; increased tail latencies for dedicated customers running long sequences.

Actions taken this week (what we did):
- Temporarily reserved 20 GPUs in asia-southeast for customer test traffic (Sofia, done).
- Manually increased burst pool in eu-west by 15% for 48 hours (Arjun, done).
- Rolled back the problematic kernel patch on 7 nodes where image pulls failed (Liam, done).
- Enabled extra logging and a short-lived debug mode on the slot allocator for one eu-west pod (Greta, in progress).

Open action items (owners and due dates):
1) Investigate and fix slot leak root cause (JIRA-INF-4223). Steps: reproduce with failing image pull, add guard to free slots on terminal failure, add integration test. Owner: Liam O'Neill. Due: 2026-04-27.
2) Implement hedging rule prototype: if regional demand variance > 15% vs baseline and sustained for > 30m, preposition 10% of burst capacity from global pool. Owner: Arjun Patel. Due: 2026-05-04.
3) Autoscaler safety-net: add cost cap circuit that prefers cheaper-quantized variants before scaling GPU count beyond threshold. Owner: Maya Chen + Product (consult). Due: 2026-05-11.
4) Prefix/KV cache telemetry: add per-tenant cache-hit heatmaps and alert when miss-rate increases > 8% within a 1h window. Owner: Greta Andersen. Due: 2026-04-30.
5) Customer communication: CS to notify affected dedicated customers about transient latency windows and mitigations applied. Owner: Sofia Ruiz (CS partner). Due: 2026-04-22.

Risks & tradeoffs:
- Prepositioning capacity reduces cold-start latency but increases committed utilization and potential cost. Need an ROI signal tied to customer SLAs and expected QPS.
- Conservative autoscaler reduces thrash but increases tail risk during large spikes; hedging rules must be conservative initially and staged via canary.
- Fixing slot leak may require transient node restarts; coordinate with on-call windows and Dedicated customers to minimize impact.

Data & instrumentation gaps identified:
- Lack of a single region-level demand variance signal — currently derived from multiple dashboards. Priority to build a unified metric (variance-over-baseline) exposed to autoscaler.
- No per-customer cache-hit alerts; hampers root cause for tail latency on long-seq workloads.

Plan for next 7 days:
- Triage and patch INF-4223 (slot leak) and run a small canary in eu-west.
- Ship hedging prototype config to staging and run chaos test with synthetic spikes.
- Instrument unified demand-variance metric and surface it in Console (basic chart + alert).
- Evaluate cost impact of current manual reservations and propose a short-term credit/billing offset for the enterprise test customer.

Notes / miscellaneous:
- Observed that PLG trial traffic tends to cluster on weekdays 13:00–17:00 UTC — we should consider time-of-day-aware hedging for eu-west and asia-southeast.
- Suggested short-term runbook addition: "when regional demand variance > 20% and p95 latency spike > 50ms, reserve N GPUs and notify CS". Drafted a runbook stub and linked above.

Next sync: 2026-04-27 11:00 UTC (weekly capacity sync).

Appendix: quick links
- INF-4223: slot leak ticket
- INF-4298: hedging rules RFC
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/318 (autoscaler smoothing changes)

Document author: Maya Chen
Reviewed by: Arjun Patel, Greta Andersen
